notes: XPression is a real-time broadcast motion-graphics/CG platform sold as a family of rackmount server "Engines" (1RU/2RU/4RU, in SDI, IP, NDI and 12G variants) plus design-only "Workflow Tools" servers with no video I/O. This entry documents the flagship 1RU 12G-SDI rendering engine, SKU XPN-1RU-12G-M9 — the configuration most commonly sold at AV retailers as "the XPression" hardware unit. Primary source: Markertek's product/spec page (a retailer explicitly acceptable per sourcing guidance), whose spec table's wording, categories, and figures (chassis, PSU, CPU/GPU, Ethernet, RS-232, USB, PS/2) match Ross Video's own manufacturer cut sheet for the related XPN-HW-CORE-V3 "XPression Workflow Tools Core Server" (fetched directly from documentation.rossvideo.com), which shares the same physical platform/control I/O. Ross Video's own cut sheet specifically for the XPN-1RU-12G-M9 engine (titled "XPression 1RU Engine Hardware Specs") could not be fetched directly (404s on current and archived URLs), so confidence is medium rather than high. Caveats: (1) SDI grade is labeled "12G-SDI" in the product title/model name but the line-card description itself just says "HD-SDI or Quad-link SDI (Matrox DSXLE4/44/100)" without an explicit per-port line-rate table, so the sdi-12g grade on the BNC ports is inferred from the model designation. (2) The 8 video BNCs are physically the compact "HD-BNC" (mini-BNC) connector style, not full-size BNC — they break out to standard BNC via supplied adapter cables; "bnc" is the closest available connector id. (3) The 4 "bidirectional" video BNCs are user-configurable per-port as input or output (used for up to 4 channels of 1080p Video/Key pairs, or 1 channel of quad-link UHD); the other 4 are fixed outputs only. (4) "USB 3.1 (Type A)" ports' generation (5Gbps Gen1 vs 10Gbps Gen2) isn't specified by the manufacturer; usb-5g (Gen1) is assumed as the common default for bare "USB 3.1" labeling. (5) Front-panel USB-C ports' speed/mode is not stated, so no grade was set. (6) The 2x "P/S2" (PS/2) legacy keyboard/mouse ports have no good match in the allowed connector list; "midi-din" was used as the closest available circular DIN-family connector — the real connector is a 6-pin mini-DIN (PS/2). (7) Audio is embedded-only in the SDI signal (no discrete analog/AES audio jacks). (8) GPI is delivered only via RossTalk over the existing Ethernet ports (no discrete physical GPI connector). (9) Other XPression chassis (2RU, 4RU, IP/NDI variants, and the Core/Core-Plus/Workstation "Workflow Tools" servers) have different port counts/types not covered here.
